beats.label: HOOK + PROMISE
beats.narration: Should you race Rule of Three? I rated 328 gravel races on 15 dimensions. Rule of Three scored 76 out of 100. Elite tier. Here's what that actually means for your season.
beats.text_on_screen: Should You Race Rule of Three?
beats.editing_note: STATE THE PREMISE IN 8 SECONDS. Clear value prop: 'I rated 328 races. Here's where this one lands.' This is the 8-second decision window. Viewers who stay past 15s are 58% more likely to finish.
beats.psych_mechanism: Curiosity gap (specific) + IKEA effect (viewer predicts the tier before reveal).

beats.label: THE COURSE
beats.narration: Rule of Three. Bentonville, Arkansas. 115 mi. A long, irregular sequence of tarmac, gravel, technical B-roads, and climby singletrack. Speed on one surface creates fatigue and handling consequences on the next. The 2027 route is not yet published.
beats.text_on_screen: Rule of Three | Bentonville, Arkansas | 115 mi
beats.editing_note: Let the course breathe. Show the route map, then cut to terrain-specific B-roll. This is the SETUP phase — grounding the viewer before the data analysis. Pacing: 25-40 sec cuts.

beats.label: THE SCORES — Top 8
beats.narration: Fourteen dimensions. Here's where it lands. Technicality. 5 out of 5. Borderline mountain bike territory. The organizer describes technical B-roads, loose gravel descents, steep singletrack, sharp rock, and roughly 25 miles of trail in the established flagship format. Adventure. 5 out of 5. Type-two fun guaranteed. Type-one fun optional. A single day that deliberately links tarmac, remote gravel and B-roads, and real singletrack creates an unusually varied challenge. Experience. 5 out of 5. This race ruins other races for you. The three-surface identity, finish-line party, unusual awards, and Bentonville setting are distinct rather than interchangeable with a standard gravel fondo. Community. 5 out of 5. The community IS the race. The organizer explicitly centers kindness, team participation, volunteers, gifts for strangers, aid-station culture, and a long finish-line gathering. Race Quality. 4 out of 5. High-quality event. Attention to detail shows. The established event pairs serious route design with aid stations, navigation instructions, team formats, and explicit safety systems. Value. 4 out of 5. Good value. More bang for your buck than most. The organizer designs sponsor participation around rider value and a full event-week experience, though the 2027 entry fee is not yet published. Logistics. 3 out of 5. Adequate. The word was invented for this. Length. 3 out of 5. Proper race distance. Enough to hurt. The established flagship is 115 miles, but the mixed surfaces make elapsed time substantially longer than an ordinary 115-mile gravel route.
beats.editing_note: PROGRESSIVE RHYTHM: start tight (15-20 sec per dimension), slow down for the most interesting scores (30-40 sec). Each score: number appears, brief pause, explanation. Avatar reacts to extreme scores (5/5 = chef_kiss, 1/5 = facepalm). RE-ENGAGEMENT at 3:00 mark: insert a surprising score reveal or a meme reaction to break the pattern.

beats.label: THE SCORES — Also Scored
beats.narration: And the rest of the scorecard. Elevation. 3 out of 5. Proper climbing. You'll earn your descents. Prestige. 3 out of 5. Respected. Not yet legendary. Field Depth. 3 out of 5. Good racing at every level. Expenses. 3 out of 5. Plan for a few hundred all-in. Climate. 2 out of 5. Mostly pleasant. Check the forecast anyway. Altitude. 1 out of 5. Sea level. Your lungs get a day off.
beats.editing_note: FAST PACING — 7 seconds per dimension. Quick-fire energy change from the deep analysis above. This is a PATTERN INTERRUPT through pacing shift.

weaknesses: The annual late route reveal complicates specific preparation
No single bike or tire choice is ideal everywhere
Navigation matters because most gravel and pavement is not marked
Spring rain can transform both B-roads and singletrack
The flagship takes much longer than an ordinary road-heavy 115-miler

beats.label: LOGISTICS
beats.editing_note: Utility section. Lower energy, practical value. Hybrid Tempo: alternate fast logistics items (10-15 sec) with slow map visuals (30 sec).

beats.label: VERDICT
beats.narration: Verdict: One Bike, Three Different Bad Ideas. Yes if mixed-surface handling, equipment compromise, and a community-first event appeal to you. The date is confirmed, but wait for the annual route release before treating any prior year's mileage, climbing, sector order, or schedule as final.
beats.text_on_screen: One Bike, Three Different Bad Ideas — 76/100
beats.editing_note: CLOSE THE MAIN LOOP. 0.5s silence before verdict. Tier badge slams in. Avatar delivers final take. DO NOT signal 'wrapping up' — maintain energy.

beats.label: ALTERNATIVES
beats.narration: If Rule of Three isn't quite right for you. Core4 uses a similarly deliberate multi-surface concept, while Big Sugar offers a larger Bentonville gravel race without making singletrack one-third of the identity.
beats.editing_note: Bonus value — viewers who reach this point are highly engaged. Cross-reference other videos/races.
